sources.title: Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue Review
sources.snippet:
Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue is a luck-based family game that, once people understand all of the cards, plays pretty quickly, but does require that all players can perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers 1-10. When math is part of the game and not just used to determine the final score, for me the game falls into the educational games, which makes it excellent for families with kids learning math and for math classes. It does not mean it will graduate to a game [...] In Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue, the rulebook states that the Queens are awake and have journeyed back to their castles to resume their normal royal lives… which makes me assume the Queens were sleeping in part one (That and the game was called Sleeping Queens). Well in this sequel the Queens are trying to rescue the Kings that have landed in some perilous predicaments. To rescue the Kings, the Queens will need to find a Rescue Companion with the same symbol in the forest. [...] 3.   Place Number cards, Spell Books, and Queens that you draw face-up in your realm.
4.   Take one or more of the following actions: 
    1.   Make a math equation with at least three of your cards and then discard the used number cards and draw a facedown Rescue Companion. (Is everyone jumping out of their seats? Math!!!)
    2.   Play a pair of number cards and wake up all of your sleeping Queens
    3.   Play a Spell Book and look through the discard pile for a number card

sources.title: Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue | Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue!
sources.snippet:
A player must discard a Queen and a Companion card that share the same symbol\icon in order to rescue a King. The Queen is placed in the discard pile and the Companion is returned to the ring of cards face-up. Face-up Companions are not allowed to be taken until all face-down cards are taken. Only then can the face-up Companions be re-shuffled and placed out in a ring to be taken again. [...] A player can take any King of their choice when they manage to rescue one. The kings have no discernible difference apart from their name and the artwork they feature. This is a departure from the original game in which Queens were worth various points). [...] The active player can then awaken one Sleeping Queen, should they have one that was put to sleep. 

Finally, the active player must roll the dice again. It is possible to roll several Dragon results in a row in this way. 

The dice distribution consists of a single 1, two 2's, two 3's and the Dragon. Image 95: Reinas Durmientes 2 ¡El rescate! Cards:strip_icc()/pic7625950.jpg)

sources.title: Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue!
sources.snippet: In Sleeping Queens 2: The Rescue, the Pancake Queen, the Ladybug Queen, and their friends return with some new characters and a new mission: save the kings!

sources.title: Sleeping Queens 2 The Rescue!
sources.snippet: In Sleeping Queens 2, roles are reversed and the queens must rescue the kings. Players take turns trying to collect queen cards and pair them with animal cards

sources.title: SLEEPING QUEENS 2: THE RESCUE CARD GAME - THE TOY STORE
sources.snippet:
The queens are awake and have journeyed back to their castles to resume their normal royal lives, but this is not a happily-ever-after story quite yet! On the way home, the kinds landed in some perilous predicaments that require the queens’ help. To rescue the kings, the queens need to first find rescue companions hiding in the forest. The first player to rescue the required number of kings wins! [...] + 2 players – rescue 4 kings
  + 3-4 players – rescue 3 kings
  + 5 players – rescue 2 kings
 Great for family game night!
 Reinforces math skills, visual discrimination, creativity and imagination!
 Includes 6 knights with stands, 1 custom die, rules of play and 94 cards:
  + 40 number cards (four of each number 1-10)
  + 12 Queens
  + 10 Kings
  + 2 turn guides
  + 6 Wild Gnomes
  + 5 Switch Witches
  + 5 Sleeping Willows
  + 4 Spell Books
  + 10 rescue companion tiles

+ Add your review [...] and first published in 2005, the game has become a world-wide best-seller. So when we heard that they made a sequel during the pandemic, we were royally excited! Packed with a mix of familiar elements and some fun new characters (hello Wild Gnomes!), and punctuated by Jimmy Pickering’s ever-charming illustrations, we hope you’ll find this game to be a worthy successor!
